**Severity:** error · **Area:** Resume (`RV2xxx`) · **Quick fix:** none

## Message

The diagnostic reads:

```text
{file} is owned by {framework} but uses the Rivet runtime ({use}): Rivet code in a framework module is never compiled by Rivet
```

Parts in braces (`{name}`) are filled in for each report.

## How to fix

Move the Rivet code (signals bound to Rivet JSX, `@rivetjs/runtime` helpers) into a Rivet module and import the island from it, or take the file out of the bridge's ownership: drop the framework suffix (`Chart.react.tsx` → `Chart.tsx`) or narrow the bridge's `include`.

## Example

```tsx avoid nocheck
// Chart.react.tsx (owned by react())
import { Show } from "@rivetjs/runtime/dom";
export function Chart() { return <Show when={true}>x</Show>; }
```

```tsx prefer
// Chart.react.tsx: React only
export function Chart() { return <div>x</div>; }
// page.tsx (Rivet): <Show when={ready()}><Chart client="visible" /></Show>
```

## When it is reported

Vite plugin (`rivet({ bridges })`). A module a bridge owns is compiled by that framework's plugins only: an `@rivetjs/runtime` import (or `@jsxImportSource @rivetjs/runtime`) there would run Rivet ABI code the Rivet compiler never produced. `@rivetjs/reactivity` signals are fine inside framework components (read them through the framework's own subscription).
